plan: [ In a 3-bidder English clock with pre-committed exit prices, bidding your true value is optimal (equivalent to a second-price auction). With independent private values, truthful bidding maximizes expected profit: shading only reduces the chance of winning and doesn’t lower the price you pay when you still win (since price equals the second-highest bid). Therefore, set the sealed bid equal to my value, $35, so I win whenever I have the highest value and pay the second-highest bid. ]

[ This is effectively a second-price auction: the ascending clock ends at the second-highest sealed bid. Truthful bidding (bid = value) is weakly dominant: - Overbidding risks winning and paying above value if a rival’s bid lies between your value and your inflated bid. - Underbidding risks losing profitable wins when the clock stops below your value. With no exploitable history and uniform independent values each round, bid my value to maximize expected profit. I will bid exactly 32.0 (allowed 0.1 increments). ]

[ This auction is strategically equivalent to a second-price auction: the sealed bid sets my exit in the ascending clock, and the winner pays the second-highest bid. With independent private values and risk neutrality, the dominant strategy is to bid my true value. Overbidding risks negative profit if I win above my value; underbidding risks losing profitable cases when rivals’ bids lie between my bid and value. My value is 48 (near the top of 0–49), so I bid 48 and accept tie-breaking if needed. ]
